newsitem.title: GERMANY: SOCCER-DORTMUND WELCOME BACK STARS FOR BAYERN CLASH.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-DORTMUND WELCOME BACK STARS FOR BAYERN CLASH.

text.p: Borussia Dortmund's injured stars are reporting back for duty at just the right time for coach Ottmar Hitzfeld -- before Saturday's crunch Bundesliga clash with Bayern Munich and next week's European Cup semifinal.
Dortmund have fallen six points behind leaders Bayern and know they cannot afford to lose Saturday's home game if they are to stand a chance of claiming their third title in succession.
"If Bayern win, then they've made it," admitted defender Juergen Kohler, just one of an expensive collection of top players who have been sidelined over the last few weeks.

Kohler, the most experienced marker in the German game, is set to return from an ankle injury which kept him out of last week's defeat away to Duisburg and the 1-0 win over Manchester United in the the first leg of the European semifinal.
Strikers Karlheinz Riedle and Stephane Chapuisat are fit again and libero Matthias Sammer will return after suspension.

Playmaker Andy Moeller has recovered from flu but fellow midfielder Paulo Sousa and wing-back Stefan Reuter are still struggling with injuries and striker Heiko Herrlich is only fit enough to take a place on the bench.
If they can stay free of injury against Bayern, Hitzfeld will have a stronger side for the game in Manchester on Wednesday than the team which played in Dortmund last week.
The coach knows the pressure is on his side on Saturday but insists a win for Dortmund would put the strain back on Bayern.
"I firmly believe we can win the championship and if we beat Bayern, then we're the favourites again," he said.

His opposite number at Bayern, Giovanni Trapattoni, has few injury worries -- international midfielder Thomas Strunz is his only doubt for the big match. Internal squabbles from earlier in the season also seem to have cleared up.

"We have all the advantages in the world," said midfielder Mario Basler, who gave a public demonstration of the new harmony in the Bayern camp by embracing Trapattoni when he was substituted during last week's 3-2 win over Cologne.

The weekend could be crucial to the outcome of the championship race as not only do Bayern take on fourth-placed Dortmund on Saturday but second-placed Bayer Leverkusen face third-placed VfB Stuttgart on Sunday.
Both sides, who failed to even qualify for the UEFA Cup last season, have mounted surprise challenges this season and still believe they have a good chance of winning the title.
"We'll have to give everything just to get a point from the game," said Leverkusen coach Christoph Daum, a master in the art of putting psychological pressure on his opponents.
For Stuttgart, the championship could be the first part of a memorable double. Joachim Loew's side reached the Cup final with a 2-1 semifinal win over Hamburg on Wednesday.
"We want the double, so we're still under pressure," admitted Stuttgart defender Thomas Berthold. "But it's pressure we've put on ourselves and you have to do that to be successful."
